subject: Private Deploy: offline upgrade criteria and operator SLA clarifications
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@horizonhealth.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com; laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@horizonhealth.com; david.bryce@consult-ops.com
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Horizon Health - Private deployment RFP (operator/upgrade questions)

Hi Marcus / Laura,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the RFP intake. We reviewed the private-deploy appendix and have a couple of open items specific to air-gapped/offline upgrade windows and operator responsibilities before we proceed to procurement:

1) During an offline (air-gapped) patch or model update, what operator-level actions are required on our side versus what Redwood performs remotely?
2) Can Redwood support a staged upgrade where the control plane stays disconnected and only model artifacts are swapped locally? If so, what are the acceptance criteria we should validate post-upgrade?
3) We need explicit SLAs for operator support during a scheduled offline upgrade (phone + remote session) and for emergency rollback windows.

Attached is the RFP section A7 and our baseline acceptance criteria doc. Please respond with the operator runbook excerpt and any constraints (KMS/HSM, signed images, hardware reboot) we should budget for.

[Attachment: RFP_HorizonHealth_PrivateDeployment.pdf (pdf, 2.1MB)]

Best,
Samira Khan
Director, IT Integrations
Horizon Health Systems
samira.k@horizonhealth.com

From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com; laura_bennett@redwood.com; procurement@horizonhealth.com
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 12:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Horizon Health - Private deployment RFP (operator/upgrade questions)

Hi Samira — thanks for the clear ask. Quick answers up front, followed by a more detailed attachment were preparing: 

- Operator responsibilities: In an air-gapped scenario, Horizon operators are responsible for physically staging artifacts and initiating the local install process. Redwood provides signed artifacts, a lightweight agent bundle (optional), and step-by-step runbook pages to validate each phase.
- Staged upgrade w/o control plane: Supported. We provide an "artifact-only" upgrade path: signed model binaries + checksum manifest + operator verification checklist. Control plane reconnection is not required for the swap; we recommend a post-upgrade reconciliation when connectivity is available.
- SLAs: For scheduled offline upgrades we offer a 4-hour remote-support window during business hours (US ET) and an on-call escalation path for critical rollbacks (target 2 hours to begin remote troubleshooting). On-site support can be quoted as an add-on.

I'm looping in Irene (solutions engineering) to attach a runbook excerpt and the acceptance criteria matrix. Laura, can you confirm whether we should include HSM notes or keep KMS-only references in the public runbook?

Thanks,
Marcus
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
[Attachment: redwood_operator_runbook_v2.pdf (pdf, 480KB)]

Subject: Re: Horizon Health - Private deployment RFP (operator/upgrade questions)

Marcus / Irene,

Appreciate the quick response. A couple of clarifying items based on your note: 

- "Artifact-only" upgrade: can you confirm the binary signing mechanism and whether our appliance can validate signatures locally with no external OCSP or certificate checks? We can't rely on outbound connectivity.
- Acceptance criteria: we'll need a short, testable checklist we can run during our UAT window. Examples: model loads in <120s, inference latency within 10% of baseline, KV/cache warming completes within N tokens.
- Rollback: in our environment, a rollback must be achievable without model re-download (i.e., we need a retained prior artifact locally). What's Redwood's recommended retention approach and disk sizing guidance?

Thanks — David (our integration consultant) also has a few kernel/driver questions that might require a deeper tech call.

Regards,
Samira

From: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com; laura_bennett@redwood.com; david.bryce@consult-ops.com
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 10:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Horizon Health - Private deployment RFP (operator/upgrade questions)

Hi Samira / David — thanks for the precise items. Technical clarifications below; I've attached an operator checklist spreadsheet with sizing guidance.

- Signing & offline validation: We sign artifacts using an offline signing key and include a signature bundle (signature + public cert). The appliance validates signatures locally using the bundled public cert; no OCSP or external certificate validation is required. We recommend storing the public cert in your local keystore (instructions in the runbook).

- Testable acceptance checklist (high level):
  * Model artifact integrity: checksum and signature verification pass (automated script)
  * Load success: model initializes and responds to a synthetic prompt within 120s
  * Latency: p50/p95 inference within 10% of published baseline for your chosen model profile
  * KV warming: prefix-caching warms to 90% within the configured token budget (script included)
  * Telemetry: local logs and delivery archive generate expected entries (no external outgoing required)

- Rollback + retention: We recommend retaining the previous N model artifacts (default N=2) on a separate volume. The checklist includes disk sizing per model (see attached). Rollback is a local command in the agent bundle; no download required if artifacts are present.

- Kernel/driver notes: We support the following minimal driver set in air-gapped installs: NVIDIA driver 525.x or newer, CUDA 11.8+, and a specific glibc set. If you have locked-down kernels, we'll provide binary compatibility notes and a compatibility shim where feasible.

Attached: privatenet_upgrade_checklist.xlsx (sizing + checklist).

Happy to schedule a 30-minute tech call with your team and David to walk the checklist. Proposed times: Wed 13 May 10:00 ET or Thu 14 May 14:00 ET. Which works for you?

Cheers,
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com
[Attachment: privatenet_upgrade_checklist.xlsx (xlsx, 95KB)]

Samira — thanks for the confirm. Quick summary & next steps so your procurement team has a single doc to reference: 

1) Offline upgrade model: Supported via signed artifact bundle + local verification. No outbound connectivity required to validate signatures.
2) Acceptance criteria: Irene's checklist (attached) is the recommended UAT slate. We will provide a one-page acceptance criteria summary for procurement to include in the SOW.
3) Retention/rollback: Redwood recommends keeping two prior artifacts; disk sizing rules are in the checklist. Rollback is a local agent command and can be initiated by your operator without Redwood network access.
4) SLAs for offline windows: Scheduled upgrade remote-support window = 4 hours business-hours response (phone/remote). Emergency rollback initiation target = begin troubleshooting within 2 hours of incident report; full timeline depends on root cause. On-site support quoted separately.

Next steps: I will upload the 1-page Acceptance Criteria summary to the deal page and share a DocuSign addendum outlining the offline upgrade support terms if Horizon is comfortable with the approach. Can procurement confirm preferred tech-call time (Irene's options: Wed 13 May 10:00 ET / Thu 14 May 14:00 ET)?

Thanks — attaching the acceptance summary and runbook excerpt for your packet.

Regards,
Marcus
